skillCheck.title: JDK, Classes, and First Output Skill Check
skillCheck.instructions: Answer ten questions grounded in this week’s five Study concepts. Seven correct answers pass. Answer choices are reshuffled for every new attempt and remain stable while that attempt is in progress.

questions.prompt: The Week 1 guide defines JDK. Which description matches that definition?

options.label: tools for compiling and running Java
a named definition containing Java members

questions.explanation: JDK means tools for compiling and running Java; it is used to use javac and java through the IDE. Avoid this mistake: install only a browser plugin.

questions.prompt: The learner needs to use javac and java through the IDE. Which concept from the Week 1 guide supports that decision?
questions.explanation: JDK is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to install only a browser plugin.

questions.prompt: During the guide's debugging drill for class, which warning identifies the error to avoid?

options.label: remove static and expect normal launch
place semicolons after every block header
save a public Main class in Other.java

questions.explanation: class means a named definition containing Java members; it is used to place main inside Main. Avoid this mistake: save a public Main class in Other.java.

questions.prompt: A classmate is about to save a public Main class in Other.java. Which concept should they review first?
questions.explanation: class is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to save a public Main class in Other.java.

questions.prompt: Which activity from the Week 1 guide correctly demonstrates main method?

options.label: use javac and java through the IDE

questions.explanation: main method means the standard application entry point; it is used to run public static void main. Avoid this mistake: remove static and expect normal launch.

questions.prompt: Which weekly concept is demonstrated by this guide activity: run public static void main?
questions.explanation: main method is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to remove static and expect normal launch.

questions.prompt: A learner must explain statement terminator before coding. Which explanation is accurate?

options.label: tools for compiling and running Java
a named definition containing Java members

questions.explanation: statement terminator means the semicolon ending most statements; it is used to write int count = 2;. Avoid this mistake: place semicolons after every block header.

questions.prompt: The guide describes "the semicolon ending most statements". Which term does it describe?
questions.explanation: statement terminator is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to place semicolons after every block header.

questions.prompt: Which mistake would show that System.out was misunderstood?

options.label: save a public Main class in Other.java
remove static and expect normal launch

questions.explanation: System.out means standard console output; it is used to use System.out.println. Avoid this mistake: expect println to read input.

questions.prompt: To avoid this error—expect println to read input—which weekly concept must the learner apply?
questions.explanation: System.out is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to expect println to read input.

builds.title: Microbuild: a labelled command-line receipt
builds.outcome: A working, tested a labelled command-line receipt.
builds.brief: Deliverable: a labelled command-line receipt. Required behavior: demonstrate JDK, class, main method, statement terminator, System.out; complete one normal, one boundary, and one invalid case; and keep a short expected-versus-actual test record. Evidence: the exact run command, the repaired defect, the three final results, and an honest README.

steps.text: Write a three-case contract for a labelled command-line receipt: one normal case, one boundary case, and one invalid case. For each, record the input or action and the expected result before coding.
Create the runnable source and implement the normal case first. Make JDK, class, main method visible in the code or interface, then run the exact launch command once.

Add the boundary and invalid-case behavior using statement terminator and System.out. Deliberately reproduce this weekly mistake—expect println to read input—record the symptom, repair one cause, and rerun the same case.
Run all three contract cases again. In README, record the environment, exact run command, expected versus actual results, repaired defect, and one known limit.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A learner can follow the README command and run a labelled command-line receipt through its stated normal case without an unexplained error.
The finished work visibly demonstrates the Week 1 concepts: JDK, class, main method, statement terminator, System.out.
The test record lists normal, boundary, and invalid inputs or actions with both expected and actual results.
The debugging note names the failing case, observed symptom, root cause, single repair, successful rerun, and one known limit.

hints: If the normal case fails, reduce it to the smallest input or action involving JDK and inspect the observed value before editing.
If the boundary or invalid case fails, revisit the guide warning "expect println to read input" and change one cause at a time.

questions.prompt: The Week 1 guide defines JDK. Which description matches that definition?

a named definition containing Java members

questions.prompt: A classmate is about to save a public Main class in Other.java. Which concept should they review first?
questions.explanation: class is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to save a public Main class in Other.java.

options.label: use javac and java through the IDE

questions.explanation: main method is the relevant concept. A common mistake is to remove static and expect normal launch.

JAVA-B-W04-01.brief: Deliverable: a reusable calculation library. Required behavior: demonstrate method, parameter, return type, overload, scope; complete one normal, one boundary, and one invalid case; and keep a short expected-versus-actual test record. Evidence: the exact run command, the repaired defect, the three final results, and an honest README.

steps.text: Write a three-case contract for a reusable calculation library: one normal case, one boundary case, and one invalid case. For each, record the input or action and the expected result before coding.
Create the runnable source and implement the normal case first. Make method, parameter, return type visible in the code or interface, then run the exact launch command once.

Add the boundary and invalid-case behavior using overload and scope. Deliberately reproduce this weekly mistake—expect a method local in main—record the symptom, repair one cause, and rerun the same case.
Run all three contract cases again. In README, record the environment, exact run command, expected versus actual results, repaired defect, and one known limit.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A learner can follow the README command and run a reusable calculation library through its stated normal case without an unexplained error.
The finished work visibly demonstrates the Week 4 concepts: method, parameter, return type, overload, scope.
The test record lists normal, boundary, and invalid inputs or actions with both expected and actual results.
The debugging note names the failing case, observed symptom, root cause, single repair, successful rerun, and one known limit.

hints: If the normal case fails, reduce it to the smallest input or action involving method and inspect the observed value before editing.
If the boundary or invalid case fails, revisit the guide warning "expect a method local in main" and change one cause at a time.
